1: Chapter 1: A Guest in the Rainy Night
In Felsheim it had been raining for three days. In spring, Anna Weber's older sister had gone to Berlin, and since then Anna had run the village's small pharmacy alone.
At nightfall she closed the shutters, counted the day's takings, blew out the lamp and went upstairs.
She had barely lain down when there was a loud knock at the door below. A man's voice called: "Is anyone there?"
A young man stood at the door, soaked to the skin, his left arm wrapped in a bloody cloth. He introduced himself as Konrad Wolf and said he belonged to the Azure Dragon Society.
"I need a bandage," Wolf said quietly. "I can pay. Will three thousand five hundred marks be enough?"
He pulled a letter wrapped in oil paper from his jacket. "This letter must be at Steinbach monastery before the eighteenth of May."
Anna must have been blind: only now did she notice how pale he was.
Nevertheless she did not take his money and said only: "Tomorrow morning I will take you into the mountains."
2: At daybreak they set out. Anna carried a basket on her back with bread, medicinal herbs, and an old umbrella.

Halfway up the mountain they met old Hans Becker, who was chopping wood. He set the axe aside and said quietly that three strangers had asked at the village entrance about an injured young man the previous evening.
"Take the path, Anna," said Hans Becker. "The country road isn't safe." Anna thanked him.
The path was narrow and slippery. Anna went ahead, placing each step carefully. Wolf followed her in silence.
By noon the rain stopped, the fog slowly lifted, and in the distance the roof of Steinbach Monastery appeared. At the gate stood a nun, Sister Hildegard, who welcomed guests at the monastery.
Sister Hildegard took the letter, examined the red seal, and nodded. "The abbess has been waiting for this letter for 2 years."
Wolf said to Anna, "I owe you my life." Anna smiled: "Then next time you can repair the roof of my pharmacy." Wolf stayed at the monastery.
In the evening Anna descended the mountain alone. When she arrived home, it was already dark; she lit the lamp and sat for a long time behind the counter.
